newsitem.title: USA: Illegal immigration, drugs up along Texas border.
newsitem.headline: Illegal immigration, drugs up along Texas border.

text.p: Illegal immigration is up 35 percent and drug smuggling has risen 25 percent so far this year in the area around the southwest Texas border town of El Paso, officials said Tuesday.

"We're going to need more people and technology," said Border Patrol Chief William Veal. "This will be critical to our success in preventing illegal crossings and stopping the trafficking of drugs and the other criminal activity that goes with it."
He said a crackdown on immigration in Arizona and California accounted for part of the increase in illegal immigration along the Texas stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border.
About 150,000 people have been arrested after crossing the border in and around El Paso, up from 111,000 arrests in the same period last year.
Border Patrol spokesman Doug Mosier said illegal immigrants were finding it harder to evade police after crossing the Rio Grande so they were turning to professional smuggling bands.
He said drug smuggling has also increased, with 970 seizures, valued at about $200 million, made so far in 1996, up from 785 in the same period last year.
